s.g: Combining form used to form prefixed perfective verbs with various transitive meanings, e.g. "instruct, give".

ety.text: Borrowed from German Aufschlag. Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *slahaną (whence English slay, slag). Doublet of аншла́г (anšlág), дуршла́г (duršlág), форшла́г (foršlág), шлаг (šlag), and шлагба́ум (šlagbáum) and more distantly doublet of шлак (šlak) and шля́хта (šljáxta).
